title: The AI influencer who had lots of us fooled
description:
There’s just SOMETHING not quite right about that French influencer we’re seeing all over socials. His blonde bob, the suit he wears, and that moustache! His name is Jean Philanthrope, and his videos have wracked up millions of views. But, it turns out, he’s not real. He’s AI and he’s being used to promote a risky type of crypto called a Meme coin.

We speak to BBC Verify’s Marco Silva about how he investigates characters like this, how they work, and what you can do to keep yourself safe from falling for this kind of content. Artist and performer Nadir Josi also tells us his concerns about the ‘copy and paste culture’ of the internet, and what it means for the future of art.

Instagram: @bbcwhatintheworld Email: whatintheworld@bbc.co.uk WhatsApp: +44 330 12 33 22 6 Presenter: Hannah Gelbart Producers: Mollie Perella Editors: Emily Horler
summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討人工智慧網紅 Jean Philanthrope 爆紅的現象，以及其帳號推廣迷因幣所引發的風險。 BBC Verify 記者 Marco Silva 分享查證過程，包括檢查平台標示與影片中突然變形的背景物件。創作者拒絕公開身分，並表示角色並非為推廣迷因幣而製作，也未收取相關推廣費用。專家提醒，迷因幣價格容易受到社群炒作影響，觀眾應查證資訊，避免因害怕錯過機會而投入無法承受損失的資金。表演者 Nadir Josi 則認為，人工智慧可協助剪輯與製作字幕，但把完全生成的內容當成真人作品販售，可能誤導觀眾並排擠真正的創作者；他主張清楚標示，讓觀眾自行判斷。
summaryEn: This episode investigates Jean Philanthrope, a viral French influencer generated by AI whose account promotes a meme coin. BBC Verify journalist Marco Silva explains how platform labels and changing objects in the background helped reveal that the videos were artificial. The creators declined to identify themselves and said the character was not created to promote the coin and that they had not been paid to promote it. Experts warn that meme coins are driven by social media hype and can change sharply in value. Listeners are encouraged to verify claims and avoid letting fear of missing out lead them to risk money they cannot afford to lose. Performer Nadir Josi describes useful AI editing tools but worries that misleading synthetic content could push real artists aside. He argues for clear labeling so audiences can make informed choices.
